Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values

Class Values

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values.Values
public final class Values extends Object
The value semantics of Mandela in one place: what a value is called, when it is true, how it prints, how it compares, how it converts and how arithmetic behaves on it.

Every runtime value is an ordinary Java object. The mapping is fixed and nothing else may claim these slots:

Mandela value to Java representation
MandelaJava
nullnull
BoolBoolean
IntLong
DoubleDouble
StrString
ListMandelaList
MapMandelaMap
RangeMandelaRange
FunCallable
declared typeMandelaInstance
ClassMandelaClass
ErrMandelaError
captured variableRef

Keeping values as plain Java objects is what makes the host boundary nearly free: a value crosses into Java without conversion, a Long becomes a Kotlin Long, and the desktop's own Swing widgets can be handed to a script unchanged.

  • Field Details

    • ABSENT

      public static final Object ABSENT
      The marker the machine leaves in a parameter slot the caller did not fill.

      A defaulted parameter is applied by the callee, because the default expression is code that may read the parameters before it. The caller therefore cannot evaluate defaults; it stores ABSENT and the prologue tests it with Op.IS_ABSENT. The marker never escapes into a script: a function called with a hole it has no default for fails at the call site.

    • isMandelaValue

      public static boolean isMandelaValue(Object value)
      Whether a value is one the machine can run on exactly as it stands.

      This is the same classification typeName(java.lang.Object) reports: anything it calls Host is a Java object the language has no meaning for. A host boundary that wants to fail early rather than deep inside a script compares against this instead of guessing.

    • fromHost

      public static Object fromHost(Object value)
      Widens an ordinary Java value into the Mandela value the machine runs on.

      Only the shapes a host reaches for without thinking are converted: the narrower number types, anything text-like, a java.util collection, an array and a map with string-ish keys. Anything else comes back unchanged, which is what lets a caller tell "already a value" from "not one" — deciding what a domain object means is a host decision, and org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.api.Interop is where the language makes it, because that is also where a function-shaped object gets its callable.

      Parameters:
      value - the candidate, possibly null
      Returns:
      the Mandela form, or value itself when there is nothing to do

    • toHost

      public static Object toHost(Object value)
      Converts a Mandela value into the plain Java form a host can hold onto.

      This is the mirror of fromHost(java.lang.Object), and it has to exist because MandelaList is only Iterable and MandelaMap is nothing at all — a host lambda declared as Function<List, …> cannot be handed a script list, however much the two look alike. A MandelaInstance reads as its field map for the same reason api.Interop.toJava does it: a host can do something with a map, and with a script object it cannot.

      The copies are deep, so a host keeping a result never keeps a live scene the script can still change underneath it. Functions, ranges and errors are passed through as themselves; they have no honest Java equivalent and a host that wants one takes it through api.Interop.

      Parameters:
      value - the value a script produced; may be null
      Returns:
      the Java form

    • truthy

      public static boolean truthy(Object value)
      The truthiness rule, chosen to match what the comparisons already say: everything except null, false, 0, 0.0 and "" is true. An empty list or map is true, because [] == [] is true and a caller must be able to keep a collection out of a boolean test by accident only when it is really a scalar.
